notes:
This is the continuation and close of the English letter begun on scan 22. The opening completes the parenthesis about embedding automorphisms of the quadruple in the group of exterior automorphisms of G. The main paragraph asks about the canonical Lie-algebra morphism and Steinberg's group morphism, their differential ranks, unipotent orbits, and varieties of Borel subgroups containing a given element. It closes “Sincerely yours” with a rightward handwritten autograph, read A G with the compressed remainder locally doubtful. There is no new date, title, salutation, authorial page number or total page count; lower-left 22 is an archival number recorded as a comment.

The rank proposal begins “There are some reasons to believe”. The text expects rank r−1 for the stated orbit dimension n−r−2 in the same-root-length case and literally writes “< r−1” in all other cases. It then says “I would expect that there is just one orbit” and “maybe this property will be caracteristic”. The Borel-variety paragraph says “I would expect the dimension of the previous variety to be equal to i” for orbit dimension 2N−2i, and “the inequality … would imply” the rationality of the indicated fibers. These qualifications remain; the sheet supplies no proofs.

The source spellings “analoguous” and “caracteristic”, unspaced “beinteresting”, “how varies”, “rang”, and singular “answer” followed by “are well known” are retained. A thin trace rises above the e of beinteresting. Cancelled this is followed by an additional cancellation x; both are retained. The raised n− and all each have a curved insertion leader. The cancelled phrase “the next lower after” and its live retyping occupy two rows. In the A/D subscripts, dimension, Brieskorn, if and then, overlapping contours do not establish a chronological order; the text preserves them as local graphics. The extra a in homogene…ous is resolved from its surviving closed bowl despite R3's retained a/u doubt. The ordinary underlined g, h and O remain distinct from H's Fraktur/script renderings. The cancelled t/star beside O is retained directly above the lowered F-prime without a mathematical role. Separate small traces in answer, at the signature, below the later W, and in the lower blank area are drawn without assigning them punctuation or a formula function.

**Actual mathematical work.** The complete internal arguments and exact computations are in `math_checks/123_023_rank_and_fiber_checks.md` and `math_checks/123_023_rank_certificate.json`, produced by `scripts/check_123_023_ranks.py`. No external source was consulted. Restricting Aut(G)→Out(G) gives the stated injection conditionally on a trivial inner stabilizer; this does not prove the preceding general apposition claim. For SL_m, Jordan-block endomorphism counts and independent power-trace differentials prove orbit dimension n−r−2 and quotient rank r−1 for the element of type (m−1,1), in the Lie algebra and at its unipotent translate. Exact calculations independently check m=2,…,6. They do not settle types D/E or orbit uniqueness.

For Sp4, the explicit matrix N with 2×2 blocks [[0,I],[0,0]] has N²=0 and orbit dimension six = 10−2−2. The symplectic weight calculation exhibits two root lengths. Both Lie-algebra and group quotient differentials have rank one = r−1; the PSp4 group quotient also has rank one at its image. Thus this example refutes the universal strict-rank expectation for the other root-length cases. That prompted a tight crop of the inequality: the ink has a plain two-stroke <, without a lower equality stroke. The source is left unchanged. The refined statement recorded in CHECK_EVENTS is only this particular C2/B2 calculation, not a classification-wide substitute.

An elementary flag argument for a rank-one square-zero element of sl3 identifies two P1 components meeting in a point, so its Borel variety has dimension one, agreeing with (6−4)/2. For the sl2 nilpotent cone, the even-degree ring k[s²,st,t²] is normal and its resolution is the total space of O on P1 of degree −2. Direct computation of the section ring and of the cohomology of O(2m), m≥0, gives f_*O=O and R^i f_*O=0 for i>0. These are actual low-rank checks. The general Borel-dimension bound, the proposed depth implication, all-fiber rationality, the D/E claims and uniqueness remain unproved background/questions in this run. Each reader additionally performed only the elementary substitution 2N=n−r, i=1, obtaining n−r−2; symbol-by-symbol reading of a theorem was not counted as a proof.

All sixteen C questions, including repeated warnings about the two subscripts and cancelled homogeneous cell, have explicit reconsideration entries. The following-cover title originally attached to the H packet was a packet-boundary error: it is excluded from this page and from the witness-change counts.
